images.name: Rover Pipeline
images.description: Rover Pipeline LLC is a large-scale interstate natural gas transmission system connecting Marcellus and Utica production in Pennsylvania and West Virginia with demand markets across Ohio, Michigan and the broader Midwest. The approximately 700-to-713-mile system has 3.425 Bcf/d of transportation capacity, is substantially contracted under long-term agreements and is operated by an Energy Transfer affiliate. The canonical PortCo is Rover Pipeline LLC; ET Rover Pipeline LLC, BCP Renaissance entities and Traverse Midstream Partners are ownership vehicles, while pipeline segments, interconnects and the separately owned Ohio River System are outside the Rover company boundary. Ares Management owns a 32.4% indirect interest through Ares Core Infrastructure Fund and the BCP Renaissance vehicles, Energy Transfer reports a 32.6% economic interest through ET Rover Pipeline LLC, and ePointZero owns 35% through Traverse. Blackstone's 32.44% indirect interest was realized when Ares acquired its vehicles on April 28, 2026. Rover's separately attributable headquarters, founding year and Energy Transfer's precise initial investment date are not publicly disclosed. No later Rover-level sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

ownershipPeriods.stake: 32.44% indirect interest in Rover Pipeline (49.9% of ET Rover Pipeline LLC, which owned 65% of Rover)

milestones.event: ePointZero closed its $2.25 billion acquisition of Traverse Midstream Partners, including Traverse's 35% non-operated interest in Rover Pipeline.

Energy Transfer signed and announced an agreement for Blackstone's BCP Renaissance vehicle to acquire 49.9% of ET Rover Pipeline LLC, equivalent to an effective 32.44% indirect interest in Rover Pipeline.

Energy Transfer closed Blackstone's 49.9% acquisition of ET Rover Pipeline LLC, establishing Blackstone's 32.44% indirect Rover interest while Energy Transfer retained an effective 32.6% interest and Traverse retained 35%.
Rover completed construction and entered full commercial service as a major Appalachian Basin natural-gas takeaway pipeline.
Ares Core Infrastructure Fund acquired Blackstone's BCP Renaissance vehicles on April 28, taking a 32.4% indirect Rover interest; Ares and Blackstone announced the completed transaction on April 29.
